output.summary: KEP-5030 proposes making cluster-autoscaler aware of CSI volume attach limits when simulating scale-up (via templated CSINode objects for upcoming nodes), and having the kube-scheduler NodeVolumeLimits plugin refuse pods needing a CSI volume on nodes lacking that driver, but only when a cluster admin explicitly opts in via CSIDriver. Status is implementable, stage beta.
output.rationale: Cluster-autoscaler ignores CSI attach limits for upcoming nodes, so it packs too many volume-using pods per node and undershoots scale-ups. The scheduler plugin also treats a missing CSINode as unlimited, letting pods land on nodes before their drivers publish. The KEP fixes CA simulation and makes the scheduler behaviour opt-in so that CA and scheduler changes stay decoupled and default behaviour is preserved.

alternatives.option: Taint new nodes and have the CSI driver remove the taint once it starts
alternatives.why_not: Listed only as an alternative in the KEP and used by some vendors; the KEP does not say why it was not chosen.

alternatives.option: Reuse the GPULabel pattern / scale-from-0 tags for node readiness
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (towca) said the GPULabel pattern is limited and cross-provider tags should not be introduced; the proposal instead defers template predictions to cloud-provider integrations via TemplateNodeInfo().

alternatives.option: Make the scheduler change on by default
alternatives.why_not: Maintainers chose to delay default enablement of the scheduler feature gate until CA changes are GA and one more release has passed, due to CA/scheduler version skew during upgrades.

alternatives.option: Node Readiness Gates proposal (kubernetes/enhancements#5233) for CSI readiness
alternatives.why_not: Described as a possible long-term solution; the author said the KEP is not blocked by it and plans to use the DRA-style design for now.

evidence.quote: Only when explicitly opted in in CSIDriver instance, the scheduler CSI plugin assumes that "no information about a CSI driver published in a CSINode" means "the node cannot handle any volumes".
For fake "upcoming" Nodes created in-memory by CA during scale-up simulations the corresponding "upcoming" CSINode is not created/taken into account.
I am proposing that - we delay beta graduation(enabled by default) of scheduler featuregate until CAS change has been made GA and one more release has passed.
predicting the CSI limits in scale-from-0 scenarios will be fully delegated to cloud-provider integrations via NodeGroup.TemplateNodeInfo()
I do think we need some form of approval from SIG scheduling though, given that there are changes in kube-scheduler proposed (however minimal).
